actions.doc: Apply a declarative content-plan tree to a site (plan.node get-or-create by site+parent+slug — naturally idempotent, never duplicates; topics/sources land as edges). Keywords and topics are plain text — resolved to existing rows or created automatically (entity-owned name resolution). One item = one site's tree.

BranchPurpose.description:
WHY a branch of the plan exists, recorded ON the branch node.

Captured at PLANNING time, when the planner still holds the whole tree in
its head and every branch point IS a decision it just made. This is
deliberately NOT a stored copy of the plan: a plan blob goes stale the
moment a user adds or removes one page, while a branch's purpose survives
every leaf change beneath it — it only dies when the branch itself does.

Downstream, placing ONE page walks UP the tree: this branch's purpose plus
its ancestors' and its aunts'/uncles' — tens of lines even on a
6,000-page plan, instead of compressing a whole site into a prompt.
